identity.title: Pericardial friction rub (triphasic scratchy sound, LSB, leaning forward, end-expiration)

technique.how: With the diaphragm pressed firmly at the left lower sternal border, listen with the patient sitting, leaning forward, in held end-expiration. A rub is a superficial, scratchy, leathery sound with up to three components (atrial systole, ventricular systole, early diastole) that persists when breathing is held; re-listen at intervals because rubs are evanescent.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room; patient able to sit forward and hold breath briefly.

interpretation.positive_finding: A pericardial rub is one of the four ESC diagnostic criteria for acute pericarditis (with typical chest pain, ECG changes, new/worsening effusion) and is essentially pathognomonic when clearly heard.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a rub does not exclude pericarditis (most patients lack one at any given exam) and a rub may disappear as effusion accumulates.
interpretation.pitfalls: Confused with pleural rubs (stop with held breath), murmurs, or stethoscope-skin artefact; rubs are intermittent so a single negative auscultation is weak evidence.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: satisfies a pericarditis criterion - get ECG and echo; negative: do not exclude pericarditis or tamponade.

sources.citation: Adler Y, Charron P, Imazio M, Badano L, Barón-Esquivias G, Bogaert J, Brucato A, Gueret P, et al. 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases. Eur Heart J. 2015.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on presence or absence of a rub to judge hemodynamic significance of an effusion.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rub plus hypotension, elevated JVP, or pulsus paradoxus suggests tamponade - urgent echocardiography.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No reliability data located; auscultatory detection is examiner- and timing-dependent.

extraction_notes: No JAMA RCE or diagnostic-accuracy meta-analysis for the pericardial rub was found; searches 'pericardial friction rub acute pericarditis prospective cohort' returned nothing usable and 'pericardial rub[Title]' returned only older case-series titles that were not fetched within budget. The 2015 ESC guideline lists the rub as one of four diagnostic criteria (2 of 4 required) but gives no sensitivity/specificity, so the record is not_quantified. The Imazio 2007 prognosis cohort (PMID 17502574, fetched) reports no rub frequency in its abstract. Frequency of rub in pericarditis cohorts (often cited as roughly one-third) is (unverified recall) and was not entered.
